tag list.

SkippedReason.description:
The reason an update check was skipped.

Programmatic consumers (JSON, scripts) can distinguish skip causes without
string parsing. JSON serialization produces a discriminated object:
- Unit variants: `{"reason": "bootstrap"}`
- Variants with detail: `{"reason": "registry_probe_failed", "detail": "…"}`

oneOf.description:
The new binary could not be started at all — it could not be resolved
out of the package just pulled, or the spawn itself failed. The inner
string carries the underlying error context.

The child ran and exited non-zero, carrying its exit code. `82`
(`DirtyRcBlock`) is the expected one: the setup completed the swap but
left a user-edited shell profile alone.

The child was killed by a signal (Unix only), carrying the signal
number.

HandoffFailure.description:
Why the hand-off to the newly pulled binary's own `ocx self setup` did not
complete cleanly.

Does not by itself mean the update was not installed: a child that failed
late may already have swapped the binary.

Serialized as a discriminated object: `{"reason": "exited", "detail": 82}`.

identifier.description: Identifier of the available update; present iff status = `update_available`.

skipped_reason.description:
Why the check was skipped; present iff status = `skipped`. Scripts
dispatch on its `reason` slug without string parsing.

UpdateCheckData.description:
Result of an update check, discriminated by `status`.

- `{"status": "up_to_date"}` — no payload
- `{"status": "update_available", "identifier": "<id>"}` — newer version
  available at `identifier`
- `{"status": "skipped", "skipped_reason": {"reason": "<variant>"[, "detail": "…"]}}`

ocx_home.description:
`$OCX_HOME`.

A missing home is an ordinary state on a fresh install and exits 0; only
a home that cannot be *read* exits 74.

shell_integration_installed.description:
Whether `ocx self setup` has ever wired this machine's shell.

Probed as the witness shim under `ocx_home`.

toolchain_home.description:
The **resolved toolchain home**, a machine-readable contract field.

The supported way for an IDE, a devcontainer feature or a CI step to find
a project's tree when `config.toml` relocates it with `toolchain_dir`:
`<project>/.ocx/toolchain` or `<toolchain_dir>/<project-key>/toolchain`
for the project in effect, and `$OCX_HOME/toolchain` when no project
resolves. **Always present, never `null`**: an invalid `toolchain_dir`
fails config load with exit 78 instead.

toolchain_bin.description:
The **PATH-facing trampoline directory** for the same tier, which a consumer outside ocx puts on `PATH`.

`toolchain_home` answers *where the tree is*; this answers *what to
export*, and the two are not one join apart, so never build this from
`toolchain_home`. Always present. It
names a directory that need not exist yet: a home that has never been
pulled reports the path it *would* hold.

activate.description:
The **effective** `activate` mode, past the whole ladder.

The flag tier (absent here), then `ocx.toml`, then
`OCX_TOOLCHAIN_ACTIVATE`, then the floor. The resolved answer, never a tier.

pinned.description:
The **effective** `pinned` value, resolved through the same ladder.

`true` means a composing emitter yields digest paths and consults no
`links/<group>/<entry>` link; `false` means it follows the rendered links, so
an `ocx update` takes effect with no re-render.

lock_refusal.description:
Why the project's `ocx.lock` refuses composition, when it does, as text.

Set when consent activates over a lock composition refuses, such as a
`paths` grant over an unreadable or stale lock. Every prompt then exits 65
and the scope never reaches the ledger.

carrier_present.description:
Whether the `__OCX_ENV_STATE` carrier is set at all.

This is what separates two inert states: an absent
carrier is the first prompt of a shell (nothing applied, nothing to
repair); a carrier that is present and undecodable is a corrupt one (a
scope was applied and its record is gone).

carrier_bytes.description: The carrier's encoded length in bytes, measured against the carrier cap.

ledger.description:
The decoded ledger, **rendered as fields, never as base64**.

Envelope tag, schema `v`, and the payload; `None` when the carrier is
absent or fails to decode. Carries what is applied per scope (`global` and
`project` separately), whether `priors` are intact for each constant the
project scope owns (the one datum nothing can reconstruct) and, through
`over_cap`, the abandoned-scope marker.

fingerprint_current.description:
Whether the ledger's recorded `fp` still matches the watch set on disk now.

`None` when there is no recorded fingerprint to compare against, **and**
when no fold is available to compare with.

watch_set.description: The watch set, with each member's presence, size and mtime.

project_dir.description: The project the CWD walk resolved, canonicalized.

project_stamped.description:
Whether a usable consent stamp exists for that key; an unusable stamp
counts as absent.

grant.description:
**Which clause activated this project**, or `None` when it is inert.

`"stamp"`, `"namespace"` or `"path"`. A consent stamp outranks the
`[shell.consent]` table.

stamp_written_at.description:
When the consent stamp was written (RFC 3339, UTC), when there is one.

The stamp's own recorded instant, not its file time. `None` whenever
`project_stamped` is `false`.

priors.description: Prior intactness for each constant the ledger's project scope owns.

hook.description: The hook's enablement and the rung that decided it.

yielded_to.description:
Every coexisting tool observed live in this shell.

One entry per observed tool; the `yielded_to` inert reason names only the
first.

inert_reason.description:
Why the shell is not active, when it is not — **the command's reason to
exist**. `None` when the project is active.

notes.description:
Reason rows that explain an answer without being an inertness verdict of
their own.

ShellStateReport.description:
What `ocx shell state` reports: all derived, none of it mutating.

Read-only: it never writes a stamp, repairs a ledger or emits a plan.
Repair is `unset __OCX_ENV_STATE` or a new shell.

oneOf.description: Compose the toolchain environment on every prompt. The default.

Put `<home>/toolchain/active/bin` on `PATH` and compose nothing else, so a
tool is resolved by its launcher trampoline at invocation time.
Neither. The reconciler withdraws whatever it owns and adds nothing.

ActivateMode.description:
How a rendered toolchain home reaches a shell's environment.

Wire values are `"env"`, `"bin"` and `"none"`; any other `ocx.toml` value
is a parse error (exit 78), never a silent default.

v.description: Schema version of the payload shape.

fp.description:
Watch-set fingerprint.

Folds the raw `OCX_CONSENT_*` values, the recorded config-tier paths and the
project's consent stamp; `verdict` expires when it changes.

verdict.description: The cached negative verdict: `inert` or `noproject`, never `activate`.

tiers.description:
The config-tier paths in effect at compose time.

An absent list falls back to re-deriving the paths. Omitted when empty.

ws.description:
Digest of the ordered watch-path list baked into the shell's emitted gate.

Omitted when empty.

messages_fp.description:
A digest of the deferred diagnostics the previous prompt printed.

Kept alongside `fp` when the carrier is over cap. Omitted when empty.

over_cap.description:
Scopes the 16 KiB cap dropped; omitted when empty.

A scope it names is reconciled exactly as an absent scope.

oneOf.description: Never written to the carrier.
The negative-consent cache, expired by the watch set.

The walk resolved no project at all; wire spelling `"noproject"`.

Entering any project expires it.

Verdict.description:
The cached activation verdict.

`activate` is never written; the watch set expires both cached verdicts, `inert` and
`noproject`.

oneOf.description: The `--global` toolchain tier.
The project resolved by the CWD walk.

ScopeId.description:
Which scope a ledger datum belongs to: `global` or `project`.

Exactly two slots. A project nested inside a project does not layer; the inner
one *replaces* the outer, so moving between them is a switch.

global.description: The global toolchain tier's applied entries.

global_priors.description:
Pre-apply values for the **global** scope's constants.

Captured against the **pre-global** environment. Omitted when empty.

value.description: The exact string ocx wrote, byte for byte.

separator.description: The effective list separator; omitted unless `type` is `list`.

LedgerEntry.description:
One env-var binding the reconciler applied, recorded literally.

Values are raw, unescaped, byte-exact copies of what ocx wrote.

`separator` holds the **effective** separator, resolved once at record time: always
present for `list` (defaulting to a single space), omitted otherwise; for `path` it
means the platform's `PATH` separator.

oneOf.description: The variable did not exist before ocx set it; reverting removes it.
The variable held this exact string; reverting restores it.

Prior.description:
What a scope's previous value was, for the constant revert path.

A set-but-empty variable is `value` with an empty string and **never** `unset`, so
reverting it restores the empty value rather than removing the variable.

key.description: The project key derived from the canonical project directory.

dir.description: The canonical project directory, advisory only.

priors.description:
Pre-apply constant values, captured against the **post-global** environment, so
reverting the project leaves the global scope standing.

ProjectScope.description:
The project scope's record.

`key` and `dir` are **advisory identity labels**, re-derived from the CWD walk every
prompt: any `dir` other than the walk's own result means the scope has been left.

mtime.description:
Modification time as whole seconds since the Unix epoch, when present —
the same granularity the per-prompt fast path compares.

WatchMember.description:
One member of the fingerprint watch set, as it stands on disk right now.

Absent members are recorded too.

oneOf.description:
Clause 1 — a valid stamp for this directory whose source set covers the
lock's. A human ran one of the stamp-writing commands here.

Clause 2 — every repository the store recorded for the lock's tools
resolves to a source matching `[shell.consent] namespaces`, bounded by
what this host actually pulled under that name rather than by what the
lock claims.

Clause 3 — the canonical directory is covered by `[shell.consent]
paths`: by an entry naming it exactly, or by a trailing-`/*` entry
naming it or an ancestor of it and granting that whole subtree. Opens
the project `[env]` channel, also for a checkout the entry never named.

Grant.description:
Which consent clause granted activation, and therefore how much it granted.

`stamp` and `path` authorize both the tool channel and the project's own
`[env]` channel; `namespace` authorizes tools only.
A `paths` entry `/w/acme/*` grants `/w/acme` and every project beneath it,
including ones that do not exist yet, but not the sibling `/w/acme-evil`;
no `*` spelling reaches the filesystem root.

key.description: The constant's env key, as the carrier records it.

intact.description: Whether a prior is still recorded for it.

PriorStatus.description:
Whether the project scope still holds the prior for one constant it owns.

Nothing can reconstruct a prior, and the `unset __OCX_ENV_STATE` repair
gesture destroys them.

rung.description: The deciding rung, rendered the way a user spells it.

tier.description: The config tier that **actually** set it, when rung 4 decided.

enabled.description:
The resolved answer, or `None` on rung 5: "auto" is decided shell-side
by the shim's interactivity probe, which a diagnostic cannot observe.

HookStatus.description:
The per-prompt hook's enablement, as its ladder resolved it.

The answer comes from rung 3 (`OCX_NO_HOOK`), rung 4 (`[shell] hook`) or
rung 5 (auto): `ocx shell state` takes no `--hook` / `--no-hook` flag.

tool.description: The tool observed live in this shell.

signal.description: The env-var evidence, rendered for a human.

Observation.description:
One live-session observation: which tool, and the signal that proved it.

`signal` is what `ocx shell state` renders: it names the variable observed and,
for direnv, the directory it named.

oneOf.description:
Yielded on `DIRENV_DIR` **naming the resolved project's canonical
directory**. A `DIRENV_DIR` naming a *different* directory is treated as
absent — direnv is active for some ancestor, not for this project.
Yielded on `MISE_SHELL` **or** `__MISE_ORIG_PATH` being present.

paths_tested.description: The `paths` entries compared against the canonical directory.

namespaces_tested.description: The `namespaces` patterns the derived sources were matched against.

oneOf.description:
No valid stamp and no matching grant — with the project's derived source
set and the grants it was tested against, so the user can see what to
add. Also surfaces a `paths` **near-miss**: an entry differing from the
canonical directory only by ASCII case.

new_sources.description: Sources present in the lock and absent from the stamp.

oneOf.description:
A stamp exists but the current lock's source set is not a subset of it —
**naming the source that is new**.

claimed_sources.description: The source set derived from `ocx.lock`'s repository fields.

verified_sources.description:
The source set derived from the store's recorded pull origins, or
`None` when no complete record exists.

oneOf.description:
Every source the lock *claims* matches `[shell.consent] namespaces`, but
the package store's record of where the locked digests came from does
not corroborate it, so clause 2 refuses.

`claimed_sources` is what `ocx.lock` says, `verified_sources` what
`refs/origins/` proves. `None` means nothing could be verified (no host
leaf, not materialized, or predating origin recording) and clears at the
next `ocx pull` — except for a digest already materialized under another
repository, which never clears. A `Some` that disagrees means a stored
digest came from a repository outside the granted namespace.

tier.description: The config tier that set it, when rung 4 decided.

oneOf.description:
The hook is disabled — naming which of the five enablement rungs decided
it and the tier that set it, including the managed tier winning over a
user's own file.

Yielded to another live per-prompt hook — naming the **live signal
observed**. One row per observed tool.

scope.description: The scope whose payload was dropped.

oneOf.description:
The ledger's payload exceeded the 16 KiB cap and this scope was
abandoned, its record lost rather than repaired.

The carrier is absent, truncated, or carries an unrecognised envelope
tag — **distinguishing** the first prompt of a shell (nothing applied,
nothing to repair) from a corrupt carrier (a scope was applied and its
record is gone).
`ocx.lock` is absent, unreadable or unparseable.

Reason.description: Why a shell is not active — the enumerated set `ocx shell state` renders.

candidate.description: The symlinked candidate that was skipped.

ancestor.description: The ancestor project activated in its place.

oneOf.description:
The CWD walk skipped a symlinked `ocx.toml` candidate and promoted an
ancestor.

Active via a `paths` grant, which is unconditional: source-set drift is
**not** tracked for path grants.

detail.description: The resolution failure, rendered for a human.

oneOf.description:
A project file was reachable but could not be resolved (an unparseable
`ocx.toml`, a canonicalization failure).

canonical.description: The canonical project directory it was compared against.

oneOf.description:
A `paths` entry that would grant `canonical` if the compare folded ASCII case.

Exact or subtree entry alike. Entries are compared as literal bytes, so
the project stays inert.

defect.description: What is wrong with the entry, rendered for a human.

oneOf.description:
A `[shell.consent] paths` entry that can never match any project by construction.

Classified from the entry's own bytes, independent of which project is in
view.

manifest.description:
The `ocx.toml` that would not parse — `$OCX_HOME/ocx.toml` for the
global tier, the project's own otherwise.

detail.description: The parse failure, rendered for a human.

oneOf.description:
The `ocx.toml` that answers for the reported scope exists but will not parse.

Its `activate` / `pinned` are then absent and the ladder answered from
`OCX_TOOLCHAIN_*` and then the floors, so a typo'd `activate = "nnone"`
fails **open**, to `env`, the most-composing mode.

Note.description:
A reason row that is not an inertness reason, because it does not make the
shell inert on its own: it explains an answer the user would otherwise get
wrong.

ocx_home.description:
`$OCX_HOME`.

A missing home is an ordinary state on a fresh install and exits 0; only
a home that cannot be *read* exits 74.

shell_integration_installed.description:
Whether `ocx self setup` has ever wired this machine's shell.

Probed as the witness shim under `ocx_home`.

toolchain_home.description:
The **resolved toolchain home**, a machine-readable contract field.

The supported way for an IDE, a devcontainer feature or a CI step to find
a project's tree when `config.toml` relocates it with `toolchain_dir`:
`<project>/.ocx/toolchain` or `<toolchain_dir>/<project-key>/toolchain`
for the project in effect, and `$OCX_HOME/toolchain` when no project
resolves. **Always present, never `null`**: an invalid `toolchain_dir`
fails config load with exit 78 instead.

toolchain_bin.description:
The **PATH-facing trampoline directory** for the same tier, which a consumer outside ocx puts on `PATH`.

`toolchain_home` answers *where the tree is*; this answers *what to
export*, and the two are not one join apart, so never build this from
`toolchain_home`. Always present. It
names a directory that need not exist yet: a home that has never been
pulled reports the path it *would* hold.

activate.description:
The **effective** `activate` mode, past the whole ladder.

The flag tier (absent here), then `ocx.toml`, then
`OCX_TOOLCHAIN_ACTIVATE`, then the floor. The resolved answer, never a tier.

pinned.description:
The **effective** `pinned` value, resolved through the same ladder.

`true` means a composing emitter yields digest paths and consults no
`links/<group>/<entry>` link; `false` means it follows the rendered links, so
an `ocx update` takes effect with no re-render.

lock_refusal.description:
Why the project's `ocx.lock` refuses composition, when it does, as text.

Set when consent activates over a lock composition refuses, such as a
`paths` grant over an unreadable or stale lock. Every prompt then exits 65
and the scope never reaches the ledger.

carrier_present.description:
Whether the `__OCX_ENV_STATE` carrier is set at all.

This is what separates two inert states: an absent
carrier is the first prompt of a shell (nothing applied, nothing to
repair); a carrier that is present and undecodable is a corrupt one (a
scope was applied and its record is gone).

carrier_bytes.description: The carrier's encoded length in bytes, measured against the carrier cap.

ledger.description:
The decoded ledger, **rendered as fields, never as base64**.

Envelope tag, schema `v`, and the payload; `None` when the carrier is
absent or fails to decode. Carries what is applied per scope (`global` and
`project` separately), whether `priors` are intact for each constant the
project scope owns (the one datum nothing can reconstruct) and, through
`over_cap`, the abandoned-scope marker.

fingerprint_current.description:
Whether the ledger's recorded `fp` still matches the watch set on disk now.

`None` when there is no recorded fingerprint to compare against, **and**
when no fold is available to compare with.

watch_set.description: The watch set, with each member's presence, size and mtime.

project_dir.description: The project the CWD walk resolved, canonicalized.

project_stamped.description:
Whether a usable consent stamp exists for that key; an unusable stamp
counts as absent.

grant.description:
**Which clause activated this project**, or `None` when it is inert.

`"stamp"`, `"namespace"` or `"path"`. A consent stamp outranks the
`[shell.consent]` table.

stamp_written_at.description:
When the consent stamp was written (RFC 3339, UTC), when there is one.

The stamp's own recorded instant, not its file time. `None` whenever
`project_stamped` is `false`.

priors.description: Prior intactness for each constant the ledger's project scope owns.

hook.description: The hook's enablement and the rung that decided it.

yielded_to.description:
Every coexisting tool observed live in this shell.

One entry per observed tool; the `yielded_to` inert reason names only the
first.

inert_reason.description:
Why the shell is not active, when it is not — **the command's reason to
exist**. `None` when the project is active.

notes.description:
Reason rows that explain an answer without being an inertness verdict of
their own.

VerboseShellState.description:
What `ocx shell state` reports: all derived, none of it mutating.

Read-only: it never writes a stamp, repairs a ledger or emits a plan.
Repair is `unset __OCX_ENV_STATE` or a new shell.

project.description: Absolute path of the `ocx.toml` this report describes.

package_settings.description:
`[package."<id>"]` resolve-time policy, keyed by the canonical author
string. Reported here because it is excluded from `declaration_hash`,
so nothing lock-derived can surface it.

StatusReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx status`.

`groups` and the maps inside it are key-sorted **objects** keyed by group
name, binding name and env key, not arrays.

error.description:
Why the lock could not be parsed. Its presence IS the unreadable state
— no separate boolean, which could only ever repeat what this key
already says. The header fields and every binding's `platforms` are
absent alongside it: nothing was read.

current.description:
`true` when the lock binds to `ocx.toml`: its stored `declaration_hash`
matches and every entry names its declared repository. `false` is the
lock `ocx pull` and `ocx exec` refuse.

declaration_hash_expected.description:
The hash recomputed from `ocx.toml` — what the lock's stored hash would
have to be for `current` to hold, so a consumer sees *why* `current` is
false without recomputing the project's canonicalization.

Both hashes cover `[tools]` and `[group.*]` only — `[env]` and
`[package.*]` are excluded by design, so an edit to either leaves
`current` true.

LockStatus.description:
The `ocx.lock` header, plus whether the lock agrees with `ocx.toml`.

Everything but `present` is absent when there is no lock — that is a valid
state (nothing has run `ocx lock` yet), not an error, so status reports it
and exits 0. Same for a lock that exists but cannot be parsed (an
unsupported `lock_version`, a corrupt file): `error` carries why, and the
header fields stay absent.

env.description: This scope's `[env]` table alone — never merged with another scope's.

GroupStatus.description:
One group's declarations. `default` is a group like any other: the
top-level `[tools]` and `[env]` tables in `ocx.toml` ARE its tools and env.

declared.description: The `ocx.toml` value for this binding, verbatim (`ocx.sh/go-task:3`).

platforms.description:
EVERY platform leaf the lock records, not the host's; `ocx inspect`
picks the host leaf.

ToolStatus.description:
One tool binding, as the two files describe it.

Absence is the signal, matching the `binaries` convention in the inspect
closure ("key absent on the wire means undeclared"):

- both keys — declared in `ocx.toml` and locked.
- no `platforms` — declared but not yet locked (added since the last
  `ocx lock`).
- no `declared` — locked but no longer declared (orphaned in a stale lock).

separator.description:
The declared separator for a `list`-typed value. `None` for every
other kind, and for a `list` that declared none — the project surface
may omit it, and what the omission inherits is decided at compose
time, which status does not do. Skipped in JSON when `None`.

value.description:
Verbatim as written: a relative `path` value stays relative. `ocx inspect`
and `ocx env` resolve it against the project root.

EnvValueOut.description: One declared environment value, normalized: `type` and `value` are always emitted.

tags.description: One row per swept tag, in the order the tags were given.

SweepReport.description:
What a `--tags` / `--tags-file` sweep did, one row per swept tag.

Plain format: a `Tag | Status | Detail` table, one row per tag in sweep
order. JSON format:
`{"schema_version":1,"command":"<command>","exit_code":<code>,
"data":{"tags":[{"tag","status","report"?,"kind"?,"message"?}]}}`.

The envelope's `exit_code` is the code the process returns, which for a
partially-failed sweep is non-zero while the document still names every tag
that succeeded — the whole point of not aborting at the first failure.

tag.description:
The tag as the caller spelled it, so the report names what was asked
for rather than what it resolved to.

status.description: What the sweep did to this tag.

report.description:
The per-reference report, verbatim. Present for every tag whose run
produced one, which includes a `failed` row carrying a partial report:
a `--signature-format both` tag where one leg landed and one did not.

kind.description:
The JSON error envelope's per-variant slug for this tag's failure,
falling back to its frozen category for errors outside the sign and
verify taxonomies. Present exactly when `status` is `failed`; the same
value the error's own JSON envelope would carry.

message.description:
Human-readable cause, sanitized for the terminal (CWE-150). Present
exactly when `status` is `failed` or `covered` — for a `covered` row it
names the tag whose run wrote the referrer, not a failure.

tags.description: One row per swept tag, in the order the tags were given.

SweepReport2.description:
What a `--tags` / `--tags-file` sweep did, one row per swept tag.

Plain format: a `Tag | Status | Detail` table, one row per tag in sweep
order. JSON format:
`{"schema_version":1,"command":"<command>","exit_code":<code>,
"data":{"tags":[{"tag","status","report"?,"kind"?,"message"?}]}}`.

The envelope's `exit_code` is the code the process returns, which for a
partially-failed sweep is non-zero while the document still names every tag
that succeeded — the whole point of not aborting at the first failure.

falling back to its frozen category for errors outside the sign and

exactly when `status` is `failed` or `covered` — for a `covered` row it
names the tag whose run wrote the referrer, not a failure.

Tags.description:
Tag listing for one or more packages, optionally including platform or variant details.

Plain format: two-column table (Package | Tag) by default, or
(Package | Platform) with `--platforms`, or (Package | Variant) with `--variants`.

JSON format: object keyed by package name; values are arrays of tags, platforms, or variants.

changes.description:
Pins whose pull identifier differs between the two locks, ordered by
`(group, name, platform)`.

unchanged.description:
Bindings this run examined and found unchanged, in the same order.

A scoped run (`-g` / positional names) lists only its own selection;
every other pin is carried forward verbatim, never re-resolved. A
whole-lock run examines everything.

metadata_changed.description:
Whether the load-bearing lock metadata moved — `declaration_hash`,
`declaration_hash_version` or `lock_version`. Advisory metadata
(`generated_at`, `generated_by`) is deliberately ignored: it moves on
every write and would make every `--check` fail.

UpdateReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx update` (and by `ocx update --check` before it
exits 65).

`tag`, and in `changes` rows also `from`/`to`, are present and `null`
rather than absent. **The payload is identical with and without
`--verbose`**: verbosity changes the plain rendering only.

group.description: Owning group — `default` for the top-level `[tools]` table.

platform.description: Canonical platform key the pin belongs to.

tag.description: The tag the declaration spells, `null` when it is digest-pinned.

from.description: Pull identifier before the update; `null` when newly pinned.

to.description: Pull identifier after the update; `null` when dropped.

BindingChange.description:
One `(group, binding, platform)` pin that moved between the predecessor
lock and the candidate.

`from` is `None` when the pin is newly introduced (a binding or a platform
the predecessor did not carry); `to` is `None` when it was dropped. Both
are the full pull identifier — `registry/repository@sha256:<hex>` — so a
consumer can feed either straight back to `ocx pull` without rebuilding it
from parts.

group.description: Owning group — `default` for the top-level `[tools]` table.

platform.description: Canonical platform key the pin belongs to.

tag.description: The tag the declaration spells, `null` when it is digest-pinned.

digest.description:
The unchanged pull identifier — the same
`registry/repository@sha256:<hex>` form `changes[].from` / `to`
carry, so the two arrays are directly comparable.

BindingState.description: One `(group, binding, platform)` pin the update left where it was.

Pins whose pull identifier differs between the two locks, ordered by
`(group, name, platform)`.

VerboseUpdateReport.description:
Report emitted by `ocx update` (and by `ocx update --check` before it
exits 65).

`tag`, and in `changes` rows also `from`/`to`, are present and `null`
rather than absent. **The payload is identical with and without
`--verbose`**: verbosity changes the plain rendering only.

subject_digest.description: Digest of the subject manifest whose signature was verified.

referrer_digest.description:
What carried the verified signature — **not always a manifest**.

The OCI referrer manifest's digest for a Sigstore bundle; the **layer**
blob's digest for a cosign simplesigning signature, however it was
found (one layer is one signature). Discriminate on
`signatures[].signature_format`, never `discovery_method`: a
simplesigning sidecar found via the Referrers API still reports a layer
digest. Addressable as `GET /v2/<name>/manifests/<digest>` only under
`signature_format == "bundle"`.

certificate_identity.description: Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description: Certificate OIDC issuer embedded in the Fulcio cert.

signed_at.description: Rekor integrated time (ISO-8601 UTC) of the signature entry.

signatures.description:
Every signature discovered for the subject.

**Absent** while empty, never `[]`: absence does not mean discovery
looked and found none.

VerificationReport.description:
Summary of a successful Sigstore verification.

JSON: `{ subject_digest, referrer_digest, certificate_identity,
certificate_oidc_issuer, signed_at }`, plus `signatures` once a discovery
pipeline populates it. Digests are always full in JSON; plain output
shortens `referrer_digest` to 12 hex.

signature_format.description: Which cosign wire shape carried this signature.

key_backend.description: What produced it: `keyless`, `file`, or a key-backend scheme.

referrer_digest.description: Digest of the referrer manifest or sidecar layer carrying it.

certificate_identity.description:
Certificate SAN (identity) embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a
key — a legal shape, not malformed input. Registry-served, so it is
untrusted input.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description:
Certificate OIDC issuer embedded in the Fulcio cert. Absent under a key.
Registry-served, so it is untrusted input.

signed_at.description:
Rekor `integratedTime`, ISO-8601 UTC.

Certificate validity is judged against this instant, never against
wall-clock now: a Fulcio certificate is valid for about ten minutes, and
this timestamp is the only proof the signature happened inside that
window. Absent when no transparency record exists (key mode without a
Rekor upload), which is legal and must be visible rather than inferred.

rekor_log_index.description: Rekor log index, the dedup key when present.

SignatureEntry.description:
One discovered, verified signature.

The per-signature view of the flat `VerificationReport` fields, plus which
wire shape carried it, how it was found, and what produced it.

oneOf.description: `GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest>` — the OCI 1.1 Referrers API.

The `sha256-<hex>` fallback referrers index a registry without the
Referrers API gets instead.
The cosign `sha256-<hex>.sig` / `.att` / `.sbom` sidecar tag.

DiscoveryMethod.description:
Where a signature referrer was discovered.

Reported verbatim on `signatures[].discovery_method`, so a caller can tell an
OCI 1.1 registry from one that only answers the fallback tag schema
without inspecting the registry itself.

VerboseVersionData.description:
Version information reported by `ocx version`.

`version` is always present. Every other key appears only when its source
data was available at build time, so a tarball-source, no-CI build emits
`version` alone. `cargo_pkg_version` appears only when it differs from
`version` (dev-deploy builds overriding it via `__OCX_BUILD_VERSION`).

```json
{
  "version":            "0.3.2-dev+20260528143045",
  "cargo_pkg_version":  "0.3.1",
  "channel":            "dev",
  "commit":             { ... },
  "build":              { ... },
  "ci":                 { ... }
}
```

VersionData.description:
Version information reported by `ocx version`.

`version` is always present. Every other key appears only when its source
data was available at build time, so a tarball-source, no-CI build emits
`version` alone. `cargo_pkg_version` appears only when it differs from

```json

  "cargo_pkg_version":  "0.3.1",
  "channel":            "dev",
  "commit":             { ... },
  "build":              { ... },
  "ci":                 { ... }
}
```

WarmedPath.description:
One pre-warmed tool: what `ocx pull` put on disk for it, and which kind of
directory that is.

A tool pre-warmed eagerly yields its package root; a tool whose `lazy-mode`
resolved to `always` yields its generated shim directory instead: its
package directory does not exist yet.
